thread:
Maya: Quick follow-up from the kernel-selection + attention-opt RFC. We need a concrete rollout plan for per-model enablement, safety layers, and deterministic fallback ordering.
Sam: +1. Key requirement: operator controls to enable/disable per-model kernels without re-deploying runtime.
Prashant: Thinking: expose three gates — global feature flag, model-level flag, and rollout percentage. Also a hard-fail safe mode for incidents.
Elena: For fallback ordering, prefer quantized kernels -> fp16 -> cpu. If quant fails, auto-fallback and emit metric `kernel_fallback.count`.
Maya: Agreed. Also want an emergency bypass that pins a model to last-known-good kernel via model registry metadata.
Sam: Implementation sketch:
```
models/{model_id}:
  runtime_policy:
    kernel_preference: ["quant", "fp16", "cpu"]
    attention_opt: {enabled: true, rollout_pct: 10}
    emergency_pin: null
```
Prashant: rollout_pct should be sampled by client request id to be stable. Add TTL for pins and commit history.
Elena: Metrics to watch during rollout: tail latency p50/p95, topk token rejection, and `fallback.rate` per-minute. Bench-bot: I'll add a dashboard.
bench-bot: Created dashboard `kernels/rollouts` and set alerts for >3% fallback rate or 15% latency increase.
deploy-bot: Rollout started for model `gpt-lite-v2` at 10% attention_opt + quant kernel on nodepool `dedicated-3`.
Maya: Nice — action items:
- Prashant: spec API for model registry fields + sampling algo (ETA EOD)
- Elena: dashboard + alerts (ETA tomorrow)
- Sam: add CLI to pin/unpin kernel (ETA 2d)
- Ops: emergency runbook to revert to pinned kernel

Sam: One more: fallback logs need to include kernel stack trace and model input hash for repro, but sanitize PII.
Prashant: Will ensure we only log hashed inputs and sample raw payloads behind a toggle.
Maya: Good. We'll track this as a post-RFC project and attach to the RFC thread. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
